Hukam Chand .........Petitioner
 Versus
Union of India and Others .......Respondents
Coram
Hon'ble Mr. Justice Sandeep Sharma, Judge.
Whether approved for reporting?

Yes. 
For the Petitioner: Mr. B.S. Chauhan, Senior Advocate, with  Mr. B.S. Attri, Advocate.

For the Respondents: Mr. Rajinder Thakur, Central Govt. Counsel,
 for respondent No.1.
 Ms. Shreya Chauhan, Advocate, for  respondent No.2.
 Mr. Vishal Panwar, learned Additional  Advocate General, for respondent No.3/State.

Precisely, the question, which needs to be determined in the instant proceedings is "whether Sub-Divisional Officer-cum- Competent Authority-cum-Land Acquisition Collector (hereinafter,
'CALA'), who after having passed Award becomes functus offico, can review the award passed by it,
in the absence of statutory powers of review under the National Highways Act, 1956, that too after a lapse of more than one year?"
2.

Precisely, the grouse of the petitioner, as has been highlighted in the petition and further canvassed by Mr. B.S. 2024:HHC:12412 Chauhan, learned Senior Counsel,
duly assisted by Mr. B.S. Attri, learned counsel representing the petitioner is that once CALA had passed Award in favour of the petitioner as well as other similarly situate persons, thereby awarding compensation for the land, in their possession as non-occupancy tenant, which ultimately came to be used for construction of National Date Of Decision: 12.11.2024 vs Union Of India And Others on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175769121/
1 Highway, coupled with the fact that project proponent i.e. National Highway had already deposited amount of compensation awarded by the CALA for disbursement of the same to the petitioner as well as other similarly situate person, there was no occasion, if any, for CALA to defeat rightful claim of the petitioner on the ground that though the land in question was in the possession of the petitioner in the capacity of non-occupancy tenant, but since he had not paid rent qua the same, he cannot claim proprietary rights qua the same in terms of Section 104 of Himachal Pradesh Tenancy and Land Reforms Act, 1972.
3.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Precisely, the facts of the case, as emerge from the record are that on 13.11.2022,
respondent No.1 vide Gazette of India, which was published in daily newspaper-The Tribune, notified that some parcel of land in district Shimla, including land of the petitioner is required to be acquired for widening/four-laning etc., maintenance,
management and operation of National Highway-22 on the stretch of 2024:HHC:12412 land from Kilometer 146.300 to Kilometer 156 i.e. from Shakral to Dhalli (Shimla bye-pass).
4. Pursuant to aforesaid notification, respondent No.3 issued notification under Section 3G(3) of National Highways Act, 1956, thereby informing all the concerned to submit their claims for compensation within a period of 21 days.

Since land of the petitioner comprised in Khasra Nos.313/1, 605/316/1, 599/311/1, 599/311/2,
599/311/3, 601/312/1, 601/312/2, 603/314/1, 606/317/1, 609/318/1, 319/1,
611/320/1, 613/343/1 & 615/344/1, total measuring 2288 square meters, situate in revenue village Chalaunti, Up-Mohal Chalaunti, Shimla (Urban), District Shimla, was also proposed to be acquired for the purposes, as notified in Gazette notification dated 13.11.2022, he also submitted his claim for compensation and also submitted copy of circle rate to respondent No.3.

On 20.01.2023, respondent No.3-CALA announced the Award of compensation No.9/2023 in respect of Up Mohal Chalaunti,
Sanjauli, Shimla, which also includes the land of the petitioner and sent the same to respondent No.2 for approval and and release of total amount of Rs.96,09,53,780/-
(including Rs.2,34,37,897/- as 2.5 administrative charges), which comprises cost of land, cost of structure, value of non-fruit trees, 100% solatium on compensation of land, structure and non-fruit trees and 12% of additional 2024:HHC:12412 compensation on land (i.e. Rs.42,73,51,200/-) w.e.f. 06.05.2022 to 20.01.2023 i.e.
for 259 days.

5. After passing of Award, as detailed hereinabove, respondent No.2 addressed a letter to respondent No.3, thereby intimating that NHAI has approved Award No.9/2023, dated 20.01.2023 for village Chalaunti, with rates of Rs.16,386/- per square meter.

Since vide Award, detailed hereinabove, CALA besides awarding compensation to the landowners had also proposed to give compensation to the non-occupancy tenant, who though were in possession of the land, but owner of the same was Government, respondent No.2 vide communication dated 11.05.2023 requested respondent No.3-CALA to submit justification for granting compensation Date Of Decision: 12.11.2024 vs Union Of India And Others on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175769121/
2 to the persons, who are in possession of the Government land.

Vide communication dated 20.07.2023, CALA addressed to Project Director, NHAI, PIU, Shimla, gave a justification for awarding compensation in favour of non-occupancy tenants by stating that against Khasra numbers, mentioned in the letter under reference, the entries of non-occupancy tenants against the Government of Himachal Pradesh were found recorded since 1956-57 and even prior to year 1956-57 and these entries are persisting in the record of right till date.

While making reference of judgment passed by this Court in Daulat Ram Vs. State of H.P., decided on 05.12.1978,
2024:HHC:12412 wherein it came to be held that under Sub-Section (3) of Section 104 of Himachal Pradesh Tenancy and Land Reforms Act, 1972, all rights, title and interest (including a contingent interest, if any), of the landowner of the land held by tenants shall be extinguished and all such rights, title and interest shall vest in the tenants free from all encumbrances created by the landowner, with effect from the date to be notified by the State Government in the official Gazette, provided that if the tenancy is created after the commencement of afore Act, the provision of this Sub-Section shall apply immediately after the creation of such tenancy.

sentences.text:
In nutshell,
vide aforesaid communication, CALA apprised Project Director, NHAI, PIU Shimla,
that since entry of tenancy existed much before the promulgation of the Act,
respondent including NHAI are estopped from questioning the tenancy, when it is so recorded in the revenue papers, which is a conclusive proof of the factum of existence of the tenancy.

CALA also submitted through aforesaid communication that once a person is entered as a tenant in the revenue record, then notwithstanding any agreement, except to the contrary, the person so entered shall become the owner by virtue of the provisions of Sub-Section (3) of Section 104 of the Act and as such, he is also entitled to compensation, as has been recorded in favour of landowners, but may be on different rates.
2024:HHC:12412 6.
While rendering justification, CALA vide communication dated 03.06.2023 and 13.06.2023 requested NHAI to deposit the amount of compensation awarded in favour of non-occupancy tenants.

In the meanwhile, petitioner herein, who otherwise stood awarded compensation on account of his land being used for construction of National Highway, as detailed hereinabove, submitted an application to respondent No.2 dated 03.10.2023, copy whereof was also endorsed to CALA, to decide his matter and release the compensation in his favour.

Vide communication dated 13.10.2023, respondent No.3 recommended to respondent No.2 for release of entire amount of compensation awarded against Award No.9 of 2023 dated 20.01.2023, at the earliest, so that same is distributed amongst the interested right-holders and possession could be handed-over accordingly.

Vide communication dated 06.02.2024, respondent No.2 gave the approval for the remaining awarded amount of Rs.32,04,20,785/- (including administrative charges for the Khasra numbers measuring 8079 square meter, which admittedly was such of the persons, who though were not owner of the land, but had acquired proprietary tenancy rights on Date Of Decision: 12.11.2024 vs Union Of India And Others on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175769121/
3 account of there being in possession of Government land in terms of Himachal Pradesh Tenancy and Land Reforms Act, 1972.
7.

sentences.text: Though respondent-NHAI after having received clarification from CALA, deposited amount of compensation qua the 2024:HHC:12412 land of non-occupancy tenants used for construction of road, but interestingly respondent No.3 instead of proceeding further in the matter for release of compensation, issued summon No.6172 to petitioner with the direction to appear in the office of respondent No.3 to state that why he be given compensation qua the land, which is not owned by him.

Now since despite there being deposit made by NHAI, amount in terms of Award No.9 of 2013 dated 20.01.2023 is not being released in favour of petitioner, he is compelled to approach this Court in the instant proceedings filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India praying therein for following main reliefs:
"(i) That writ of certiorari may kindly be issued, quashing and setting aside the impugned summon dated 14.02.2024 (Annexure P-10).
(ii) That writ of mandamus may kindly be issued, directing the respondents to release the compensation amount with respect to acquisition of his land comprised in Khasra No.313/1, 605/316/1, 599/311/1, 599/311/2, 599/311/3, 601/312/1, 601/312/2,
603/314/1, 606/317/1, 609/318/1, 319/1, 611/320/1, 613/343/1 & 615/344/1, total measuring 2288 square meters, situated in revenue village Chalaunti, Up-Mohal Chalaunti, Shimla (Urban), District Shimla alongwith interest @ 18% from the date of passing of the Award No.9/2023, dated 20.01.2023 till actual payment."
8.
Pursuant to notices issued in the instant proceedings, respondent-State has filed reply wherein facts, as have been taken note hereinabove are not in dispute, rather stand admitted.

Attempt has been made to defeat the claim of the petitioner on the ground that 2024:HHC:12412 though petitioner herein was non-occupancy tenant on the land in question, but since he had not deposited rent/lagaan, he cannot be said to have acquired proprietary rights in terms of Section 104 of Himachal Pradesh Tenancy and Land Reforms Act, 1972.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 9. While referring to the reply filed by respondent No.3, Mr. Vishal Panwar, learned Additional Advocate General though fairly admitted factum with regard to acquisition of land in possession of the petitioner in the capacity of non-occupancy tenant, but he submitted that as per latest Jamabandi for the year 2018-19, land in question is recorded in the ownership of State Government and the petitioner has been recorded as non-occupancy tenant without mentioning his rent/lagaan.

He submitted that as per provisions contained under Section 2(17) of the Himachal Pradesh Tenancy and Land Reforms Act, 1972, a person who holds land under a landowner would be liable to pay rent for that to landowner and further the rent means whichever is payable to the landowner in money or kind by a tenant on account of the use or occupation of land held by him.

entities.text: Himachal Pradesh Tenancy and Land Reforms Act, 1972
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
He submitted that for creation of tenancy, relationship of landlord and tenant is essential, but since in the case at hand, at no point of time, rent was ever paid, rather column of rent is blank, petitioner herein cannot be termed as tenant and as such he is not entitled to compensation qua the land, which Date Of Decision: 12.11.2024 vs Union Of India And Others on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175769121/
4
admittedly belong to State of Himachal Pradesh.

It clearly emerges from the pleadings, as adduced on record, that Khasra numbers qua which Award No.9 of 2023 stands passed also includes the land of the petitioner, which was acquired for purpose of construction of National Highway.

It is also not in dispute that possession of land comprised in Khasra No.313/1, 605/316/1, 599/311/1, 599/311/2, 599/311/3, 601/312/1, 601/312/2,
603/314/1, 606/317/1, 609/318/1, 319/1, 611/320/1, 613/343/1 & 615/344/1, total measuring 2288 square meters, situate in revenue village Chalaunti, Up-Mohal Chalaunti, Shimla (Urban), District Shimla, was very much in possession of the petitioner in the capacity of non-occupancy tenant.
Though revenue record annexed with the petition reveals that land, detailed hereinabove, is shown to be owned by State of Himachal Pradesh, but admittedly it was in the possession of petitioner.

As per own communication dated 20.07.2023, which came to be issued in reference to letter dated 23.05.2023 issued by Project Director, NHAI, PIU, Shimla, land qua which petitioner is seeking compensation, was found to be recorded in the possession of petitioner as non-occupancy tenant.

As per afore communication, the entries of non-occupancy tenants against the Government of Himachal Pradesh were found recorded since the year 1956-57 and even prior to year 1956-57 and such entries continue to exist even in Jamabandi 2024:HHC:12412 for the year 2018-19, as is evident from the reply filed by respondent No.3 (Annexure R-1).
11.
It is also not in dispute that in terms of Award No.9 of 2023 dated 20.01.2023 passed by respondent No.3, even non- occupancy tenants are entitled to compensation, but on different rates.

In the instant case, vide Award, detailed hereinabove, landowners, be it original landowners or non-occupancy tenant, came to be held entitled for compensation at the rate of Rs.16386/- per square meter.

Though, at first instance, respondent-NHAI had some reservation with regard to amount, if any, payable to non-occupancy tenant on the ground that land in question is owned by Himachal Pradesh, however, subsequently after receipt of communication dated 20.07.2023, where respondent No.3 itself clarified that even non- occupancy tenant, who with the efflux of time have acquired tenancy rights are entitled to compensation, NHAI proceeded to deposit amount of compensation with respondent No.3 for disbursement of same in favour of non-occupancy tenants including petitioner.

12. Though at one hand, CALA-respondent No.3 itself called upon Project Director, NHAI to deposit amount in terms of Award dated 20.01.2023 for release of same in favour of non-occupancy tenant along with other private landowners, but now after deposit of aforesaid amount, effort is being made to defeat the rightful claim of 2024:HHC:12412 the petitioner on the ground that there is no relationship of tenant and landlord inter se State of Himachal Pradesh and non-occupancy tenant,
especially petitioner in whose favour, Award already stands passed by the competent authority i.e.
CALA itself.

13. If the communication dated 20.07.2023 (Annexure P-6) is read in its entirety, it clearly emerges that CALA-respondent No.3 itself having perused revenue record and taking note of judgment passed by this Court in Daulat Ram's case (surpa) had arrived at a conclusion that once person is Date Of Decision: 12.11.2024 vs Union Of India And Others on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175769121/
5 entered as a tenant in the revenue record, then notwithstanding any agreement, etc. to the contrary,
the person so entered shall become the owner by virtue of the provisions of Sub- Section (3) of Section 104 of the Act, if it is so, though entry in the revenue record of the petitioner may be in the name of non-occupancy tenant, but by operation of law, it has already become owner and as such,
entitled to amount of compensation, as awarded in his favour vide Award No.9 of 2023 dated 20.1.2023.
Though pursuant to aforesaid clarification, respondent-NHAI has already deposited amount, but interestingly, same is not being released in favour of the petitioner, that too on flimsy grounds.
14. By way of filing reply to the writ petition, attempt has been made by CALA to carve out altogether a new case.

As has been noticed hereinabove, there is no denial, if any, to the fact that petitioner herein 2024:HHC:12412 has been shown to be non-occupancy tenant in the revenue record, but since column of rent/lagaan is shown blank in the Jamabandi for the year 2018-19, he is not being held entitled for compensation on the ground that since no relationship of tenant and landlord ever existed inter se State of Himachal Pradesh and petitioner, he cannot be granted compensation qua the land, which he alleged to have been in possession, on account of his being non-occupancy tenant
, however, such plea of respondent/State being totally frivolous deserves to be rejected outrightly.

If the afore stand put forth by respondent/State is perused vis-a-vis communication dated 20.07.2023 (Annexure P-6), this Court is persuaded to agree with Mr. B.S.
Chauhan, learned Senior Counsel representing the petitioner that frivolous ground has been raised by respondent/State to defeat the rightful claim of the petitioner, who admittedly, has been shown to be non-occupancy tenant against the Government since the year 1956-57 and even prior to year 1956-57, which fact itself has been clarified by the CALA in afore communication addressed to Project Director, NHAI, while making request to deposit the amount of compensation awarded qua the land occupied/possessed by non-occupancy tenants.

Once it is not in dispute that petitioner was in possession of land, detailed hereinabove, prior to promulgation of Himachal Pradesh Tenancy and Land Reforms Act, 1972, as has been clarified vide communication dated 20.07.2023 (Annexure P-6), coupled with the judgment dated 2024:HHC:12412 05.12.1978 passed by this Court in Daulat Ram's case (supra), wherein it came to be clarified that under Sub-Section (3) of Section 104 of the Act, all rights, title and interest (including a contingent interest, if any) of the landowner of the land held by tenants shall be extinguished and all such rights, title and interest shall vest in the tenants free from all encumbrances created by the landowner created by landowner, there can be no occasion for respondent No.3 to claim at this state stage that since petitioner herein failed to pay the rent/lagaan, he cannot claim to have acquired proprietary rights.

Though factum with regard to existence of landlord and tenant relationship stand duly established on record, but even if it is presumed that no rent/lagaan was paid, such fact may not be of any consequences for the reason that Section 3 of Himachal Pradesh Abolition of Land Revenue or Uneconomic Land Holdings Act,
1977, clearly provides that notwithstanding anything contained in the Himachal Pradesh Land Revenue Act, 1953 (6 of 1954), the land revenue on uneconomic holdings shall stand abolished from Rabi 1977, and the landowner who at the commencement of this Act holds uneconomic holding,
shall not be liable to pay any land revenue in respect of his land holding to the State.

sentences.text: 15. Section 2(b) defines uneconomic holding, which means a land holding which does not exceed two and a half acres and comprises of unirrigated cultivated land or of such land which has been recorded as 'banjar kadim', 'banjar Jadid' or grass lands, 'ghasnis', 'kharetars', 'rutas', etc., but does not include land under orchards or built-up areas assessed to land revenue.

Admittedly, in the instant case, land which is claimed to be occupied by petitioner as non-occupancy tenant is 'ghasnis',
meaning thereby same falls under the definition of uneconomic holding.

Section 3 of aforesaid provision of law clearly provides that uneconomic land holding shall stand abolished from Rabi 1977; and the landowner who at the commencement of this Act holds uneconomic holding, shall not be liable to pay any land revenue in respect of his land holding to the State.

Though, with the promulgation of Himachal Pradesh Tenancy and Land Reforms Act, 1972, all rights, title and interest of landowner of the land held by tenants had extinguished and land in question had vested in tenant free from all encumbrances created by the land owner, but even if it is presumed that at relevant time, land had not vested in petitioner on account of his being non-occupancy tenant, on account of his having not paid rent, he had become owner of the land 2024:HHC:12412 in question Date Of Decision: 12.11.2024 vs Union Of India And Others on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175769121/
7 free from all encumbrances.

sentences.text:
16. There is another aspect of the matter that whether it is open for respondent No.3 to review the Award passed by it, in the absence of statutory power of review under the National Highways Act,
1956, that too after a period of more than one year.

Section 3G empowers competent authority under Land Acquisition Act i.e. CALA to pass award qua land used for construction of National Highway, but definitely there is no provision under afore Act, which empowers competent authority i.e. CALA to review its award.
2024:HHC:12412 17.

In the instant case, though no formal order thereby reviewing the Award, inasmuch as debarring petitioner herein to the amount of compensation to which he already stand entitled in terms of Award No.9 of 2023, dated 20.01.2023, has been passed by CALA, but as has been taken note hereinabove, rightful claim of the petitioner has now being sought to be defeated by CALA itself by filing reply to the petition stating therein that since there was no relationship of landlord and tenant inter se State of Himachal Pradesh and petitioner, it cannot be said to have been acquired proprietary rights in terms of Section 104 of Himachal Pradesh Tenancy and Land Reforms Act,
1972.

Though in earlier part of judgment, this Court has clarified that petitioner herein has already acquired proprietary rights in terms of Section 104 of Himachal Pradesh Tenancy and Land Reforms Act, 1972 and is squarely falls in the definition of 'landowner' and as such entitled to compensation,
but even otherwise, ground sought to be raised by respondent No.3 to defeat the rightful claim of the petitioner, cannot be permitted to be defeated on the afore ground, especially when it has no authority whatsoever to review its own Award, wherein it has already held petitioner as well as other similarly situate person entitled to compensation on account of the land in their possession, may be in the capacity of non-occupancy tenant.
2024:HHC:12412 18.

sentences.text: At this stage, it would be apt to take note of judgment passed by Hon'ble Apex Court in case titled as Naresh Kumar and Others Vs. Government (NCT of Delhi), (2019) 9 SCC 416, wherein it has been held that power of review is not inherent.

entities.text: Naresh Kumar and Others Vs. Government (NCT of Delhi), (2019) 9 SCC 416
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It can be exercised only when statute provides for the same expressly/specifically or by necessary implication.

In afore judgment, Hon'ble Apex Court has held that in absence of any such provision in statute concerned, power of review cannot be exercised in case of judicial/quasi judicial orders, rather, exercise of such power in absence of express provision would be ultra vires, illegal and without jurisdiction.

Relevant Para of the afore Date Of Decision: 12.11.2024 vs Union Of India And Others on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175769121/

"13.

sentences.text: It is settled law that the power of Review can be exercised only when the statute provides for the same.

In the absence of any such provision in the concerned statute,
such power of Review cannot be exercised by the authority concerned.

This Court in the case of Kalabharati Advertising vs. Hemant Vimalnath Narichania (2010) 9 SCC 437, has held as under:
"...12.

sentences.text: It is settled legal proposition that unless the statute/rules so permit, the review application is not maintainable in case of judicial/quasijudicial orders.

In the absence of any provision in the Act granting an express power of review, it is manifest that a review could not be made and the order in review, if passed, is ultra vires, illegal and without jurisdiction.
(Vide Patel Chunibhai Dajibha v. Narayanrao Khanderao Jambekar [AIR 1965 SC 1457] and Harbhajan Singh v. Karam Singh [AIR 1966 SC 641] .)

sentences.text: It must be conferred by law either expressly/specifically or by necessary implication and in the absence of any provision in the Act/Rules, review of an earlier order is impermissible as review is a creation of statute.
Jurisdiction of review can be derived only from the statute and thus, any order of review in the absence of any statutory provision for the same is a nullity, being without jurisdiction.

14. Therefore, in view of the above, the law on the point can be summarised to the effect that in the absence of any statutory provision providing for review, entertaining an application for review or under the garb of clarification/modification/ correction is not permissible."

19. In similar facts and circumstances, Division Bench of High Court of Madhya Pradesh, while deciding Writ Petition No.8178 of 2020, titled as Indrakala Agarwal Vs. State of M.P. and Others,
2021 SCC OnLine MP 767, reiterated that unless statue provides for power of review, an award once passed in itself becomes final.

From the reading of the aforesaid judicial pronouncements of the various High Courts as also of the Hon'ble Supreme Court a fact which stands established is that unless the provision of law i.e. the statute provides for the power of review, an award once passed in itself becomes final.

The position of Law also gets well settled on the basis of the aforesaid judicial pronouncements that the power of Date Of Decision: 12.11.2024 vs Union Of India And Others on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175769121/
9

A review is always considered to be a creature of statute and the power of review cannot be entertained in the absence of a provision thereof .

20. As regards the objection of the respondents, so far as the right of the petitioners to challenge the award by way of an arbitration invoking Section 3G(5) of the National Highways Act, 1956 is concerned, this Court is of the opinion that, once when the challenge is made to the amended award primarily on the ground of, lack of jurisdiction and competence on the part of the prescribed authority, in reviewing his award and the ground being that of the authorities being denuded of their power of review this Court is of the opinion that under such circumstances, this Court in exercise of its powers under Article 226 of the Constitution of India exercising the power of judicial review can entertain a writ petition in this regard, even in the case,
if there is a provision of appeal provided under the statute.
It is by now a well settled proposition of law that when a challenge to an order is primarily on the ground of jurisdiction and competence of the authority Writ Court can entertain a writ petition.
Thus, the objection so far as the petitioners having an alliterative remedy stands rejected.

21. For all the aforesaid reasons, the writ petition deserve to be and are accordingly allowed and the impugned amended award (Annexure P/1) dated 01.06.2020 is held to be bad in law, illegal and without jurisdiction and are accordingly set-aside thereby entitling the petitioners the benefit as per the original award dated 07.03.2019."

20 . Reliance is also placed upon judgment passed by High Court of Bombay in Writ Petition No.5286 of 2018, titled 2024:HHC:12412 Bhupendrasingh Vs. Competent Authority and Others,
2019 SCC OnLine Bom 6092,

"28.

The net result of the discussion, as made above, is that the provisions of section 33 of the Act of 2013, are not available to the Competent Authority constituted u/s.
3(a) of the NH Act, 1956, in the process of acquisition of land under the NH Act, 1956 and 15 thus, it is impermissible for the Competent Authority to make any correction or for that matter to pass any order in the nature of correction of an award or for that matter an amended award.
Once the award has been passed by the Competent Authority, the Competent Authority loses any authority to tinker with it in any 20 manner whatsoever."

21. Reliance is also placed upon recent judgment of Bombay High Court in Writ Petition No.5327 of 2022, titled as Sau. Sangeeta Natwarlal Karwa and Another Vs. State of Maharashtra and Others,
wherein having taken note of its earlier judgment passed in Bhupendrasingh's case (supra), High Court of Bombay held that once the award has been passed by the competent authority, the competent authority loses any authority to tinker with it in any manner whatsoever.

sentences.text: A Division Bench of this Court in case of Bhupendrasingh vrs. Competent Authority and Others (2020) AIR Bombay R 645 2024:HHC:12412 has held that the provisions of Section 33 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short "Fair Compensation Act, 2013") are not available to the Competent Authority constituted under Section 3(A) of the National Highways Act, 1956 in the process of acquisition of the land under the National Highways Act, 1956 and thus it is impermissible for the Competent Authority to make any correction or for that matter to pass any order in the nature of correction of an award or for that matter an amended award.

18. It is further opined that none of the First, Second and Third Schedules to the Act of 2013 contemplate or take into its compass or relate to, the provisions of Section 33 of the Act of 2013.

This Court accordingly held that it would, thus, be apparent that neither the Amendment Ordinance No. 9 of 2014 nor the notification dated 28th August, 2015 make the provisions of section 33 of the Act of 2013, applicable to acquisition proceedings under the National Highways Act, 1956, in absence of which,
it cannot be held that the Competent Authority under the National Highways Act,
1956, would have any power or authority to either correct the award for any reason whatsoever or for that matter, to pass an additional award or to review the same.
19.
In our view, the principles laid down by the Division Bench of this Court in case of Bhupendrasingh (supra) apply to the facts of this case.

The National Highways Act,
1956 being the self-contained code, the provisions of Section 33 of the Fair Compensation Act, 2013 granting the limited powers in respect of the award declared under the provisions of the Fair Compensation Act, 2013 cannot be extended to the award declared under the provisions of the National Highways Act, 1956.
We do not propose to take a different view in the matter.
The supplementary award is thus totally without jurisdiction and deserves to be quashed and set aside."

It is quite apparent from the aforesaid exposition of law taken into consideration that CALA which has power to pass award under National Highways Act under Section 3G has no power to review its award, if it is so, it cannot otherwise take/raise objections which are now being sought to be raised by filing reply qua the entitlement of the petitioner for his land, which admittedly came to be used for construction of National Highway.
23.

At this stage, though Mr. Vishal Panwar, learned Additional Advocate General while referring to Section 33 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, attempted to argue that the authority responsible for issuing the Award is Date Of Decision: 12.11.2024 vs Union Of India And Others on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175769121/
11 entitled to rectify any error in its decision, however, upon a thorough examination of the aforesaid provision of law, this Court is of the opinion that the National Highways Act, 1956, constitutes self-contained statutory framework.

by its express terms, grant any authority to CALA to review or modify its own award.

. Leaving everything aside, this Court having taken note of facts and circumstance of the case,
which are detailed hereinabove, has no hesitation to conclude that for no cogent and convincing reason, rightful claim of the petitioner is being denied by CALA, which at one point of time, not only had espoused the cause the petitioner, but had compelled NHAI to deposit amount of compensation.

Now once NHAI has deposited amount of compensation in terms of award passed by CALA, coupled with the fact that CALA has no authority to review its own award, prayer made on behalf of the petitioner deserves to be allowed.
25. Consequently, in view of detailed discussion made hereinabove as well as law taken into consideration, this Court finds merit in the present petition and accordingly, the same is allowed.
Respondent No.3 is directed to release the Award amount in favour of petitioner in terms of Award No.9 of 2023, dated 20.01.2023, forthwith, along with up-to-date interest.

opennyai_summary.issue:
Precisely, the question, which needs to be determined in the instant proceedings is "whether Sub-Divisional Officer-cum- Competent Authority-cum-Land Acquisition Collector (hereinafter,
'CALA'), who after having passed Award becomes functus offico, can review the award passed by it,
in the absence of statutory powers of review under the National Highways Act, 1956, that too after a lapse of more than one year?"
2.
opennyai_summary.facts: In the instant case, vide Award, detailed hereinabove, landowners, be it original landowners or non-occupancy tenant, came to be held entitled for compensation at the rate of Rs.16386/- per square meter.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
13. If the communication dated 20.07.2023 (Annexure P-6) is read in its entirety, it clearly emerges that CALA-respondent No.3 itself having perused revenue record and taking note of judgment passed by this Court in Daulat Ram's case (surpa) had arrived at a conclusion that once person is Date Of Decision: 12.11.2024 vs Union Of India And Others on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175769121/
5 entered as a tenant in the revenue record, then notwithstanding any agreement, etc. to the contrary,
the person so entered shall become the owner by virtue of the provisions of Sub- Section (3) of Section 104 of the Act, if it is so, though entry in the revenue record of the petitioner may be in the name of non-occupancy tenant, but by operation of law, it has already become owner and as such,
entitled to amount of compensation, as awarded in his favour vide Award No.9 of 2023 dated 20.1.2023.
, however, such plea of respondent/State being totally frivolous deserves to be rejected outrightly.
Once it is not in dispute that petitioner was in possession of land, detailed hereinabove, prior to promulgation of Himachal Pradesh Tenancy and Land Reforms Act, 1972, as has been clarified vide communication dated 20.07.2023 (Annexure P-6), coupled with the judgment dated 2024:HHC:12412 05.12.1978 passed by this Court in Daulat Ram's case (supra), wherein it came to be clarified that under Sub-Section (3) of Section 104 of the Act, all rights, title and interest (including a contingent interest, if any) of the landowner of the land held by tenants shall be extinguished and all such rights, title and interest shall vest in the tenants free from all encumbrances created by the landowner created by landowner, there can be no occasion for respondent No.3 to claim at this state stage that since petitioner herein failed to pay the rent/lagaan, he cannot claim to have acquired proprietary rights.
Though factum with regard to existence of landlord and tenant relationship stand duly established on record, but even if it is presumed that no rent/lagaan was paid, such fact may not be of any consequences for the reason that Section 3 of Himachal Pradesh Abolition of Land Revenue or Uneconomic Land Holdings Act,
1977, clearly provides that notwithstanding anything contained in the Himachal Pradesh Land Revenue Act, 1953 (6 of 1954), the land revenue on uneconomic holdings shall stand abolished from Rabi 1977, and the landowner who at the commencement of this Act holds uneconomic holding,
shall not be liable to pay any land revenue in respect of his land holding to the State.
Admittedly, in the instant case, land which is claimed to be occupied by petitioner as non-occupancy tenant is 'ghasnis',
meaning thereby same falls under the definition of uneconomic holding.
Section 3 of aforesaid provision of law clearly provides that uneconomic land holding shall stand abolished from Rabi 1977; and the landowner who at the commencement of this Act holds uneconomic holding, shall not be liable to pay any land revenue in respect of his land holding to the State.
Though, with the promulgation of Himachal Pradesh Tenancy and Land Reforms Act, 1972, all rights, title and interest of landowner of the land held by tenants had extinguished and land in question had vested in tenant free from all encumbrances created by the land owner, but even if it is presumed that at relevant time, land had not vested in petitioner on account of his being non-occupancy tenant, on account of his having not paid rent, he had become owner of the land 2024:HHC:12412 in question Date Of Decision: 12.11.2024 vs Union Of India And Others on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175769121/
7 free from all encumbrances.
After promulgation of afore Himachal Pradesh Abolition of Land Revenue or Uneconomic Land Holdings Act, 1977, which clearly provided that land revenue of uneconomic holding shall stand abolished of Rabi 1977, and the landowner who at the commencement of this Act holds uneconomic holding, shall not be liable to pay any land revenue in respect of his land holding to the State, meaning thereby, in any eventuality, petitioner herein had become owner of the land in question in terms of Section 104 of Himachal Pradesh Tenancy and Land Reforms Act, 1972, which came into force on 03.10.1975, if it is so, petitioner cannot be deprived of Award which already stands passed in his favour, that too by the respondent No.3, who now has taken u-turn to defeat the rightful claim of the petitioner.
In the instant case, though no formal order thereby reviewing the Award, inasmuch as debarring petitioner herein to the amount of compensation to which he already stand entitled in terms of Award No.9 of 2023, dated 20.01.2023, has been passed by CALA, but as has been taken note hereinabove, rightful claim of the petitioner has now being sought to be defeated by CALA itself by filing reply to the petition stating therein that since there was no relationship of landlord and tenant inter se State of Himachal Pradesh and petitioner, it cannot be said to have been acquired proprietary rights in terms of Section 104 of Himachal Pradesh Tenancy and Land Reforms Act,
1972.
Though in earlier part of judgment, this Court has clarified that petitioner herein has already acquired proprietary rights in terms of Section 104 of Himachal Pradesh Tenancy and Land Reforms Act, 1972 and is squarely falls in the definition of 'landowner' and as such entitled to compensation,
but even otherwise, ground sought to be raised by respondent No.3 to defeat the rightful claim of the petitioner, cannot be permitted to be defeated on the afore ground, especially when it has no authority whatsoever to review its own Award, wherein it has already held petitioner as well as other similarly situate person entitled to compensation on account of the land in their possession, may be in the capacity of non-occupancy tenant.
2024:HHC:12412 18.
It can be exercised only when statute provides for the same expressly/specifically or by necessary implication.
In afore judgment, Hon'ble Apex Court has held that in absence of any such provision in statute concerned, power of review cannot be exercised in case of judicial/quasi judicial orders, rather, exercise of such power in absence of express provision would be ultra vires, illegal and without jurisdiction.
(Vide Patel Chunibhai Dajibha v. Narayanrao Khanderao Jambekar [AIR 1965 SC 1457] and Harbhajan Singh v. Karam Singh [AIR 1966 SC 641] .)
In Patel Narshi Thakershi v. Pradyuman Singhji Arjunsinghji [(1971) 3 SCC 844 :
AIR 1970 SC 1273] , Major Chandra Bhan Singh v. Latafat Ullah Khan [(1979) 1 SCC 321] , Kuntesh Gupta (Dr.) v. Hindu Kanya Mahavidyalaya [(1987) 4 SCC 525 : 1987 SCC (L&S) 491 : AIR 1987 SC 2186] , State of Orissa v. Commr. of Land Records and Settlement [(1998) 7 SCC 162] and Sunita Jain v. Pawan Kumar Jain [(2008) 2 SCC 705 : (2008) 1 SCC (Cri) 537] this Court held that the power to review is not an inherent power.
review is not an inherent power, it must be conferred by law either specifically or by necessary implication.
A review is always considered to be a creature of statute and the power of review cannot be entertained in the absence of a provision thereof .
It is quite apparent from the aforesaid exposition of law taken into consideration that CALA which has power to pass award under National Highways Act under Section 3G has no power to review its award, if it is so, it cannot otherwise take/raise objections which are now being sought to be raised by filing reply qua the entitlement of the petitioner for his land, which admittedly came to be used for construction of National Highway.
23.
The provisions of Section 33 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, which confer limited powers regarding the correction of awards issued under that Act, cannot be extended to awards made under the National Highways Act, 1956, meaning thereby that the latter Act does not,
by its express terms, grant any authority to CALA to review or modify its own award.
Now once NHAI has deposited amount of compensation in terms of award passed by CALA, coupled with the fact that CALA has no authority to review its own award, prayer made on behalf of the petitioner deserves to be allowed.
